To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a tyrosyl protein kinase is present in extracts of Burkett lymphoma cell lines and B cells of normal human origin, and that the 47Kd tyrosyl protein kinases from these two cell lines are different.
the pp47src protein of B cells is modified in Burkilt lymphoma cells.
the 47 Kda tyrosine kinase from Burkitt cells differs in phosphorylation, overall charge and antigenic properties from the same protein isolated from B cells of healthy individuals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the purification, characterization and expression of a tyrosine kinase in Burkitt lymphomas.
the purification and characterization of tyrosine protein kinases from Burkitt lymphoma cell lines.
the purification and characterization of proteins that are associated with tyrosine protein kinases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 47 KDa tyrosine protein-kinase is present in both B lymphocytes and Burkitt lymphoma cell lines, and that the enzyme in the latter is modified.
a tyrosin protein kinase is modified in Burkits lymphoma cells.
the pp60src gene product is modified in Burkilt lymphoma cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified an oncogene in Burkitt lymphomas.
the pp60src protein kinase is not the only protein kinase in human B lymphocytes that is related to the products encoded by the src family of transforming genes.
the 47 kDa protein is a normal protein which is phosphorylated on tyrosine residues in normal B cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 47Kd protein from Burkitt cells and the 47K protein from normal B lymphocytes have different properties.
the protein kinase in Burkitt lymphomas is not the same as the one in normal cells.
